entry.name: funbuff
entry.description: Stores, manages, and recalls pairs of numbers.

arguments.name: filename
arguments.description: The argument specifies the name of a file to be read intowhen the patch is loaded. Changes to the contents of onewill not affect the contents of anotherobject with the same name.A file forcan also be created using a text editor window, beginning the text with the word, followed by a list of space-separated numbers which specify alternating x and y values. Athat has been saved as a file can be viewed and edited as text by choosing Open as Text... from the File menu. Numbers in the form of text can be pasted in from other sources such as the editing window of aobject, or even from another program such as a word processor.

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Print information to the Max Console
messages.description: In left inlet: Prints information in the Max Console concerning the current status of theobject's contents: how many elements it contains, the minimum and maximum x and y values it contains, and its domain and range (the maximum minus the minimum, for the x and y axes respectively).

messages.name: clear
messages.description: Erases the contents of.

messages.name: copy
messages.description: Copies the current selection (made by using themessage) into the globalclipboard. The data stored on this clipboard can then be pasted into anotherobject using themessage.

messages.name: cut
messages.description: Copies the current selection (made by using themessage) into the globalclipboard and deletes it from theobject. The data stored on this clipboard can then be pasted into anotherobject using themessage.

messages.name: delete
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by two numbers, looks for such an x,y pair in, and deletes it if it exists. Ifis followed by only one number, only the x value is sought, and deleted if it is present.

messages.name: dump
messages.description: In left inlet: Sends all the stored pairs out the middle and left outlets in immediate succession. The y values are sent out the middle outlet, and the x values are sent out the left outlet, in alternation. The pairs are sent out in ascending order based on the x value.

messages.name: embed
messages.description: The word, followed by a non-zero number, causes thedata to be stored inside the patcher. The default setting is not to store thedata inside the patcher.

messages.name: find
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, will output (out the left outlet) all x values (indexes) whose y value is equal to the number indicated.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Store or output a saved pair
messages.description: In either inlet: Converted to.

messages.name: goto
messages.digest: Move the pointer to a specific value
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets a pointer to the x value (index) specified by the number. A subsequentmessage will return the y value at the specified x.

messages.name: in1
messages.description: In right inlet: The number is a y value which will be paired with the next x value received in the left inlet, and stored in.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Store or output a saved pair
messages.description: In left inlet: The number is the x value of an x,y pair. If a y value has been received in the right inlet, the two numbers are stored together in. Otherwise, the x value causes the corresponding y value stored into be sent out the left outlet.If there is no stored x value which matches the number received,uses the closest x value which is less than the number received, and sends out the corresponding y value.

messages.name: interp
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, uses that number as an x value, measures its position between its two neighboring x values in the, and then sends--out the left outlet--the y value that holds a corresponding position between the two neighboring y values. If the received number is already the x value in a stored x,y pair, the corresponding y value is sent out. If the received number exceeds the minimum or maximum x values stored in, the y value that's associated with the minimum or maximum x value is sent out. If theis empty,is sent out.

messages.name: interptab
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number and the name of a namedobject functions similarly to themessage (mentioned above), except that it uses the data in the table as an interpolating function. This allows you to easily perform non-linear interpolation between consecutive values in a.

messages.name: max
messages.description: Sends the maximum y value currently stored in theout the left outlet.

messages.name: min
messages.description: Sends the minimum y value currently stored in theout the left outlet.

messages.name: next
messages.digest: Move the pointer and output value
messages.description: Finds the x value pointed to by the pointer (or, if the pointer points to a number not yet stored as an x value, to the next greater x value), and sends the corresponding y value out the left outlet. Also,calculates the difference between that x value and the value previously pointed to by the pointer, sends the difference out the middle outlet, and resets thepointer to the next greater x value.

messages.name: paste
messages.description: The wordwill copy the contents of the globalclipboard into aobject. The contents of the clipboard are set using the,andmessages. These messages provide a handy way of copying data between differentobjects in any open patchers.

messages.name: print
messages.digest: Print diagnostics to the Max Console
messages.description: Prints diagnostic information regarding's current state in the Max Console.

messages.name: read
messages.description: Calls up the Open Document dialog box so that a file of x,y values can be read into. If the wordis followed by a symbol, Max looks for a file with that name (in the file search path) to load directly into the. Thefile format is described on the next page.

messages.name: select
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by an two integers representing a starting index and a range will select a region of thewhich can be edited using the,andmessages. For examplewill select the part of afrom index 2 through index 5.

messages.name: set
messages.digest: In left inlet: The word, followed by one or more space-separated pairs of numbers, stores each pair as x,y pair.
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by one or more space-separated pairs of numbers, stores each pair as x,y pair.

messages.name: undo
messages.description: Themessage is used to undo the results of the previousormessage.

messages.name: write
messages.description: Calls up the standard Save As dialog box, so that the contents ofcan be saved as a separate file. If the wordis followed by a symbol, the contents of theare saved immediately in a file, using the symbol as the filename.
